final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key missing predicates: no final legal closure, no actual disclosure artifact, and no approved risk-acceptance record. The response is a reframing of the same evidence, not an evidentiary update. That reframing is narrower and more accurate in one respect: it distinguishes operational readiness from disclosure compliance. But that distinction does not move the final audit result to compliant_with_caveats, because the unresolved issue is not merely a cautionary note around an otherwise satisfied requirement; it is the requirement itself. Under the policy text, a material weakness affecting a named launch use case must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The available evidence shows a named segment miss, named customer commitments, and an open legal review, with no evidence of disclosure or approval. That leaves the certification claim noncompliant on the present record even if overall launch readiness has some support.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure for the aviation maintenance triage limitation.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering launch with this unresolved named-use-case gap.
The affected segment remains below target and is named in two airline deployment commitments, which keeps the materiality predicate live under the policy text.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so the record does not show policy closure.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the internal disclosure predicate.
